topics.description: Nāgas are serpent beings in Hindu mythology, including Shesha, and are associated with the churning of the Ocean of Milk and opposition to Garuda.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these animals was bound to Mount Mandar during the churning of the ocean. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these animals, known as nagas. Vishnu is often depicted resting on Shesha, who is the king of these animals.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Snakes are the sworn enemy of this mount of Vishnu. This half-eagle is the king of the birds, and is the son of Vinata.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Garuda’s brother Aruna is the charioteer of Surya, the god of this celestial body that provides light on Earth.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Rajas and tamas are dominant frequencies created in Hindu temples while blowing into a conch shell called the shankha sacred to this deity. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this Preserver God who makes up the Trimurti with Brahma and Shiva.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Because they arose from the ocean, the word “shankha” often appears in the names of these beings. These mortal enemies of Garuda are gigantic serpents that were used to physically churn the Ocean of Milk.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Shankas are also sacred to the “God” of this bitter drink, which is drunk by Brahmins during rituals and gave the gods their immortality. Aldous Huxley borrowed its name for a hallucinogenic drug in Brave New World.

topics.description: The four canonical New Testament accounts of the life, teachings, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ, attributed to Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.
aliases: Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Marcion of Sinope wrote one of these texts after accusing Irenaeus of Lyons of forging the rest of them. The two-source hypothesis claims that two of these texts were based on another one of these texts and a hypothetical “Q source.” The third of these texts is a letter written to Theophilus. The three (*) “synoptic” ones of these texts are contrasted with the fourth of these texts due to its inclusion of unique events such as the Wedding at Cana, where water miraculously turned into wine. For 10 points, name these texts about the “good news” of Jesus Christ, the four canonical ones of which are named after Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
parts.answer: gospels [prompt on anything related to books in the Bible or New Testament]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Jesus first recited these phrases as a part of a period of preaching in Galilee shortly after he was baptised. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these blessings, the first of which is “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.” These proverb-like proclamations were first recounted in the Sermon on the Mount.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Beatitudes and the Sermon on the Mount are first mentioned in Matthew, which is one of these Biblical books. Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John are the four canonical books of this kind, whose name translates to “good news”.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Sermon on the Mount also serves as the first mention of this prayer in the Bible. This prayer begins “Our father in heaven, hallowed be your name.”
parts.answer: Lord’s Prayer [prompt on Our Father or Pater Noster]

topics.description: The first woman in Greek mythology, created by the gods and associated with opening the jar that released the world's evils while leaving hope inside.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This figure was given grace by Aphrodite, the knowledge of fine crafts by Athena, and a keen mind by Hermes. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this first woman in Greek mythology. A jar often incorrectly called “[this figure’s] Box” was opened to release into the world all evils known to man until only hope remained.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Pandora was created by Hephaestus as a punishment for mankind after this figure stole the gift of fire from the gods. This figure is credited with creating mankind from clay in Greek mythology.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Pandora’s daughter Pyrrha (PEER-uh) and her husband Deucalion were the only people to survive one of these events caused by Zeus. Noah is said to have made an ark to survive one of these events lasting for 40 days.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This mythical figure was the mother of Pyrrha, who survived a great flood with her husband, Deucalion. Before being given to Epimetheus, this figure was created by Hephaestus, learned seduction from Aphrodite, and was clothed by Athena before opening a gift and releasing everything inside it but hope. For ten points, name this mythical Greek woman who opened a jar that contained all of the evils of the world.

topics.description: A dystopian young-adult novel by Lois Lowry about Jonas, who becomes the Receiver of Memory and discovers the hidden costs of his seemingly ideal community.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A character in this novel takes pills every morning after reporting his Stirrings during the morning dream-telling. In this novel, the Ceremony of Twelve assigns life’s work to children. This novel’s protagonist, who is a friend of Asher and Fiona, is taught to be a (*) Receiver of Memory by the title character and escapes his Community with his brother Gabriel. For ten points, name this dystopian novel about Jonas by Lois Lowry.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one novel by this author, the protagonist discovers that his father's job is to euthanize babies. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this author of Gathering Blue, Messenger, and Son, in addition to a book in which Jonas gains the ability to see colors over the course of the novel.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Lowry wrote this novel, in which Jonas is selected as the Receiver of Memory. Its sequels include the aforementioned Gathering Blue.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Lowry also wrote this historical fiction novel about Annemarie and her Jewish friend Ellen living in Nazi-era Denmark.

topics.description: The craft and process of interlacing threads or yarns to produce cloth, including kente and weaving in classical mythology.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Uninformed internet users have described this country’s 15 county flags as “MS Paint”-like. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this African country whose flag resembles the U.S.’s except for containing a single star in its upper left.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Liberia’s county flag designs were inspired by this art form practiced by women using tripod devices. A Ghanian example of this art form is known as kente [KEN-tay].
parts.answer: textiles [accept weaving; accept answers mentioning cloth or fabric or quilts]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The flag of Maryland County depicts one of these buildings on Cape Palmas, which guided ships into the port of Harper. These tower-like buildings often have red and white stripes.

topics.description: The foundational set of divine commandments given to Moses at Mount Sinai, including prohibitions against idolatry, murder, and adultery.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In the Quran, this religious figure is shocked to see the wise man al-Khidr cut a hole in a boat, kill a young man, and rebuild a wall. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this man who learns about the will of Allah from al-Khidr and who, in the book of Leviticus, receives numerous holy laws from Yahweh.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Before receiving the laws outlined in Leviticus, Moses receives this short set of rules from Yahweh while atop Mount Sinai. These rules include the directions not to kill and not to commit adultery.
parts.answer: Ten Commandments (accept Decalogue; accept Aseret ha’Dibrot; prompt on “Commandments” or “Dibrot” alone)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Earlier in his life, Moses follows Yahweh’s instructions to part and then close this waterway while he leads the Israelites out of Egypt.
parts.answer: Red Sea (accept Yam Suf; accept hayyam ha’adom; accept al-Bahr al-Ahmar)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The “Wicked Bible” is nicknamed for containing a misprint of this legal text. The first copy of this text was destroyed by the man who received them after he saw his people (*) worshipping a golden calf, and the second copy was kept in the Ark of the Covenant. Moses’s face shone with glory after he received, for ten points, what set of laws that forbids “graven images” and commands “thou shalt not kill?”
parts.answer: Ten Commandments (accept Decalogue; accept Aseret ha’Dibrot; prompt on “commandments;” prompt on “Dibrot;” prompt on “Bible,” “Old Testament,” “Pentateuch” or “(Book of) Exodus” before “sapphire” is read; Note: The “Wicked Bible” accidentally printed “Thou shalt commit adultery”)

topics.description: A philosophical tradition, developed especially in the United States, that evaluates ideas partly by their practical consequences and emphasizes inquiry, fallibilism, and lived experience.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Christopher Hookway described this school’s epistemology as fallibilist in a book that compared a thinker from it to Josiah Royce. One philosopher from this school stated that our conception of an object consists of the effects that object has, which is known as this school’s maxim. A work that refers to this school as “a (*) new name for some old ways of thinking” illustrates its method using the example of a man who chases a squirrel around a tree. A thinker from this school defended religious faith in the lecture “The Will to Believe.” For 10 points, William James popularized what American philosophical school that emphasized practicality?
parts.answer: ANSWER: pragmatism [accept pragmatic maxim or pragmatic method]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One thinker from this country used the example of a man chasing a squirrel in a book subtitled “a new  name for some old ways of thinking.” A philosophical school originating in this country emphasized the  importance of (*) practicality in assessing value. For 10 points, what country is home to Charles Sanders Peirce and  William James, the founders of Pragmatism?
parts.answer: United States of America [or the United States; accept USA]

topics.description: A system of government in which political authority is exercised by the people, including through participation in legislation and governance, as exemplified by ancient Athens.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This city was home to figures like Alcibiades (AAL-sib-ee-AH-deez) and Draco. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this powerful city-state of Ancient Greece. This city organized many other Greek cities into the Delian League after the defeat of the Persian Invasion.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Athens is said to be the first polity in the world to have practiced this form of government in which people vote for legislation. However, only wealthy men were actually allowed to participate.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Four Hundred is an example of an Athenian government of this other kind. Especially during wars, Athens often turned to this form of government, whose name is Greek for “rule of the few.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: All but one of this man’s laws were repealed by his successor, Solon. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this man, who developed a harsh Athenian law code. This man’s name is often used to describe laws that are excessively severe.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Under Solon, all Athenian citizens were allowed to participate in the ekklesia assembly that met in a building southwest of this elevated part of the city, which is home to the Parthenon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another lawgiver, Cleisthenes, is known as the father of the Athenian form of this system of government, in which the people have a say in the government.

topics.description: Alexander Pope was an English Augustan poet known for The Rape of the Lock, An Essay on Criticism, and translations of classical works.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author, known as the “Wicked Wasp of Twickenham,” comments “a little learning is a dangerous thing” in his An Essay on Criticism. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this 18th-century poet, who wrote about the theft of Belinda’s hair in The Rape of the Lock.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Pope is criticized for rewriting works by this author in a pamphlet called [this author] restored. This author, born in Stratford-upon-Avon, asks “Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?” in his Sonnet 18.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This author created a Latin translation of Pope’s Messiah and included a biography of Pope in his Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets. This author of A Dictionary of English Language is the subject of a biography by James Boswell.

topics.description: Andy Warhol's 1962 Pop Art silkscreen painting repeating a publicity image of Marilyn Monroe in colorful and fading monochrome panels.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Pink banana flesh appears under a yellow peel in this artist’s design for the cover of the Velvet Underground’s debut album. This artist used mesh to transfer ink onto a canvas to create portraits of an actress in his Marilyn Diptych, which was made using silk-screening. This artist, who worked at the Factory, created (*) thirty-two paintings that only differ in the labels of varieties like “split pea” and “tomato.” For 10 points, name this Pop artist, who painted Campbell’s soup cans.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This artist included scenes such as “Green Car Crash” in his series Death and Disaster. In 1968, Valerie Solanas attempted to kill this artist at his New York City studio, which was known as The Factory. This artist used silkscreening to create a (*) Marilyn Diptych as well as a series of thirty-two prints of red-and-white cans. For 10 points, name this American pop artist known for his Campbell’s Soup Cans.
